Welcome to Rise

A space to explore, understand, and reconnect with yourself.

Rise Somatic Therapy was created from a belief that meaningful therapy honors the whole person — mind, body, emotions, relationships, and lived experiences.

My approach is compassionate, collaborative, and trauma-informed. I believe you are the expert on your own experience, and therapy should provide space to explore, understand, and reconnect with yourself without judgment.

My Story & Mission

Why I created Rise

Marie Clifton, LCSW, LSCSW — founder of Rise Somatic Therapy.

Rise Somatic Therapy was shaped by both my professional experience and my own journey through experiences that challenged my sense of safety, identity, and voice. I know what it can feel like to lose connection with yourself while navigating difficult relationships, trauma, and seasons of profound change.

Those experiences deepened my understanding that healing is not simply about knowing why we feel the way we do — it can also mean learning to trust ourselves, reconnect with our bodies, and recognize the wisdom within us. As a therapist, I wanted to create a space where people feel seen, respected, and empowered to explore their experiences without judgment.

To me, Rise represents the process of reclaiming what may have been lost, reconnecting with who you are, and finding the courage to rise into a life that feels more fully your own.

My mission

To offer compassionate, trauma-informed therapy that honors each person's autonomy, identity, story, and capacity for change.

You don't have to become someone else to heal. You can reconnect with yourself, rise from within, and move forward in your own way.

Credentials

Marie Clifton, LCSW, LSCSW

Licensure

Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) and Licensed Specialist Clinical Social Worker (LSCSW), providing virtual therapy to clients in Kansas and Missouri.

Approach

Compassionate, collaborative, and trauma-informed — integrating somatic and embodied therapy, EMDR, trauma-conscious yoga, ACT, DBT, and trauma-informed therapy as appropriate to each client.

How I Can Help

Services & Approach

Each person's path looks different. I draw from the modalities below to meet you where you are and support the work that feels most meaningful to you.

  • INDIVIDUAL THERAPY

    Support for adolescents and adults

    Navigating trauma, relationships, body image, identity, and life transitions.

  • SOMATIC & EMBODIED THERAPY

    The connection between body and mind

    Exploring the connection between your body, emotions, thoughts, and experiences.

  • EMDR

    Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing

    Supporting the processing and integration of distressing traumatic experiences.

  • TRAUMA-CONSCIOUS YOGA

    Gentle, choice-based movement

    Body awareness incorporated when clinically appropriate.

  • ADDITIONAL APPROACHES

    ACT · DBT · Trauma-Informed Therapy

    Drawn on as needed to support your specific goals and history.

Areas of Focus

Rise may be a good fit if you're navigating:

  • Trauma & complex trauma
  • Anxiety & depression
  • Relationship trauma
  • Domestic abuse
  • Body image & distorted eating
  • Eating-disorder recovery
  • Nervous-system regulation
  • Difficulty connecting with or trusting your self & body
  • Identity exploration & life transitions
  • Grief & loss
  • LGBTQ+ affirming care
  • Emotional regulation

If You Need Support Right Now

Crisis & Emergency Resources

Rise Somatic Therapy is not an emergency or crisis service, and messages sent by email or through the client portal are not monitored continuously. If you are in crisis or experiencing a medical or mental health emergency, please use one of the resources below.

  • Emergency: Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department for immediate medical or mental health emergencies.
  • 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: Call or text 988 for 24/7 crisis support, including emotional distress, suicidal thoughts, or mental health concerns.
  • Domestic Violence: National Domestic Violence Hotline — Call 800-799-SAFE (7233) or text START to 88788 for confidential support and safety planning.
  • Eating Disorders: National Alliance for Eating Disorders — Call 866-662-1235 for support, resources, and treatment referrals.
  • Mental Health & Substance Use: SAMHSA National Helpline — Call 800-662-HELP (4357) for treatment information and referrals.
  • Grief & Loss: For support during overwhelming grief or loss, call or text 988 or connect with a local grief support group or counselor.
